title: Open WebUI shared chat -- T1005 self-shared file_id grants access to a file the caller never owned
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-54010 (GHSA-vrhc-3fr6-pc3c,
CVSS 8.3 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI prior to 0.9.6.

Open WebUI lets an authenticated user attach an arbitrary `file_id`
value to their OWN chat message without checking whether they actually
own or can read that file -- the attachment step trusts the caller's
claim. An attacker who knows (or guesses) a victim's file id can attach
it to their own message, then SHARE that chat and grant themselves read
access to their own shared copy. At that point, `has_access_to_file()`
treats the victim's file as accessible THROUGH the shared chat -- and
the file endpoints then read or DELETE the victim's file, all without
ever having had legitimate access to it in the first place. The
ownership check that should have blocked the initial attachment never
ran; the shared-chat access-grant machinery downstream simply trusted
that the attachment was legitimate.

Detection logic flags a chat-share-then-file-access sequence: a chat
containing a `file_id` attachment, followed by that chat being shared,
followed by a file endpoint request against the same `file_id` from
the sharing user -- the specific ownership-bypass chain this advisory
describes, distinct from ordinary legitimate file sharing where the
attaching user actually owned the file to begin with.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.6.
